name: Trane Technologies plc
headquarters: Registered in Swords, Co. Dublin, Ireland; US operational headquarters in Davidson, North Carolina
employees: approximately 44,000 in 62 countries, including over 16,000 outside the United States (31 December 2025)
summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: Trane Technologies is a $21.3bn applied-HVAC manufacturer whose commercial business has been re-rated by data-centre demand — order backlog rose 70% year on year to $12.1bn by Q2 2026 with Applied bookings up 130% for a fourth consecutive quarter above 100% — while the company discloses no data-centre revenue figure of any kind and its residential business simultaneously weakened through a regulated refrigerant transition. BACKGROUND. The listed entity is the former Ingersoll-Rand plc, incorporated in Ireland in 2009 and renamed in February 2020 after spinning off its Industrial segment to Gardner Denver in a Reverse Morris Trust; the retained Climate business began trading as TT on 2 March 2020. It reports three geographic segments — Americas $17,168.8M, EMEA $2,802.1M and Asia Pacific $1,351.0M in FY2025 — with the Americas alone at 80.5% of revenue. Two strategic brands: Trane for commercial and residential heating, cooling and ventilation (with American Standard Heating & Air Conditioning alongside it), and Thermo King for transport refrigeration. FY2025 revenue was $21,321.9M, up 7.5%, with GAAP continuing EPS of $13.14 and adjusted continuing EPS of $13.06 — an inversion, with GAAP above adjusted, traceable to non-cash contingent-consideration adjustments that reduced expense by $61.2M. Collection gap: the company publishes no split of revenue between commercial HVAC, residential HVAC and transport refrigeration, and 'data center' appears in the FY2025 10-K only four times, all inside an alphabetical product list.
ecosystemRole: The chiller and thermal-plant layer of the data-centre cooling chain, and the equipment-side counterpart to the operator-side cooling material already in this corpus. Where Vertiv's dossier covers the room and the coolant distribution unit and Schneider's covers the building system, Trane covers the machine that actually rejects the heat and, since 2026, the distribution equipment between that machine and the rack: it acquired the direct-to-chip and immersion specialist LiquidStack in March 2026 and the modular cooling-plant business Stellar Energy in February 2026 for $553.4M gross, and it sells coolant distribution units of its own at up to 14 MW. Its ecosystem position is unusual in one respect worth stating plainly — despite a backlog driven by data-centre orders, no public source names a single hyperscaler, colocation operator or general contractor as a Trane customer. The only two publicly stated commercial relationships in this ecosystem are reference-design collaborations with NVIDIA (October 2025) and Eaton (August 2026).

productsAndServices.name: CenTraVac water-cooled centrifugal chillers
productsAndServices.description: The flagship large-tonnage line, catalogued at 120 to 4,000+ tons (450 to 14,000+ kW) at 50 and 60 Hz across models CVHE, CVHF, CVHG, CVHH and the dual-compressor Duplex variants CDHF, CDHG and CDHH. The company states the product line provides more than 200,000 individual unit selections. The architecture's defining claim is mechanical simplicity: 'The CenTraVac chiller has only one primary moving part — a single rotating shaft supported by two bearings. This direct drive concept minimizes the chance of failure by reducing the number of critical parts — no gear boxes, couplings, extra shafts, or shaft seals.' Trane traces low-pressure refrigerants in its centrifugal design to the first Trane centrifugal chiller in 1938. 'Series E' and 'Duplex' are not separate families: Series E denotes the large-tonnage CVHH and CDHH models, and the CD prefix denotes the dual-compressor variants.
highlights: Full-load efficiency, quoted verbatim: 'selectable at an unmatched efficiency level of 0.45 kW/ton at standard AHRI conditions… averaging at least 13.5 percent better than the next best centrifugal chiller available today'

Refrigerant leak rate, quoted verbatim: 'the industry's lowest documented refrigerant leak rate — less than 0.5 percent annually versus the industry-accepted rate of 2.0 percent', backed by a Leak-Tight Warranty the company describes as the first offered by any HVAC manufacturer

Refrigerants are ultra-low GWP: R-514A across the line, with R-1233zd(E) an option on CDHH and CVHH. Both are stated at a GWP 'of less than two', and R-1233zd(E) is classified A1 — nonflammable — under ASHRAE Standard 34

Heat recovery is a catalogued mode with a stated efficiency penalty: 'Typical catalog efficiencies for heat recovery machines operating in the heat recovery mode range from 0.64 to 0.84 kW/ton… and range from 0.54 to 0.57 kW/ton for a cooling-only machine'

Certified to AHRI 550/590 (I-P) and ANSI/AHRI 551/591 (SI) — with the catalogue naming explicit exclusions from that certification: free cooling, low-temperature applications below 36 °F including ice storage, machines above 3,000 tons, heat recovery and heat pump ratings, auxiliary condenser, and glycol and brines

Disclosure boundary: the catalogue publishes flow-rate tables but no per-model IPLV, NPLV, kW/ton or sound data — selection is routed to Trane Select Assist software. This is a deliberate first-party gap rather than an omission
productsAndServices.positioning: Independent share data places Trane second in data-centre chillers at 18.7% of a $2.6bn 2025 market behind Johnson Controls at 20.9%, ahead of Carrier at 14.5%, Daikin at 12.0% and Vertiv at 8.1% (Global Market Insights, August 2026). A separate US all-end-market chiller ranking places Daikin first and Trane second without publishing percentages (MarketsandMarkets, July 2026).
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct sales and service organisation plus consulting-engineer specification — applied equipment is engineered into a building rather than bought off a shelf.
productsAndServices.roadmap: Ongoing migration of the portfolio to next-generation low-GWP refrigerants, which the company describes as the industry's transition 'from HCFCs and HFCs to next-generation, low-GWP refrigerants'.

productsAndServices.name: Air-cooled chillers — Ascend, Sintesis, CGAM
productsAndServices.description: The air-cooled range spans roughly 20 to 550 tons across three families. Ascend covers ACR (150-550 tons, screw), ACS (140-230 tons, scroll with intermediate discharge valves) and ACX (80-230 tons, vapour-injection scroll air-to-water heat pump). Sintesis RTAF covers 115-500 tons on helical rotary screw with R-513A. CGAM covers 20-130 tons on scroll compressors with R-454B. The Ascend ACR is the technical flagship, built around what Trane calls AdaptiSpeed technology — 'the integration of an adaptive frequency drive efficiently tuned to match perfectly the permanent magnet compressor motors'.
highlights: Efficiency against code, quoted verbatim: 'Over 18% better full load efficiency than ASHRAE 90.1-2016 Path B' and 'Over 22% higher IPLV than ASHRAE 90.1-2016 Path B'

Motors: 'The compressor's and condenser fans' permanent magnet motor design is up to 4 percent more efficient than conventional induction motors'; the 150 to 300 ton units use variable volume ratio semi-hermetic direct-drive rotary screw compressors

Sound is engineered and sold in tiers: 'Integral compressor muffler lowers sound levels by 4-10 dB compared to previous design'; optional metallic discharge and suction bellows 'reduce compressor sound by 8-10 dB'; three levels of sound reduction are offered
Refrigerant charge: 'Up to 40% lower refrigerant charge compared to previous evaporator designs'
Electrical: available with passive harmonic filtering achieving 5% total demand distortion, to comply with IEEE 519

Ambient envelope is a purchasable option set, quoted verbatim: standard 32 to 105 °F, low ambient 0 to 105 °F, extreme low ambient -16 to 105 °F (150-300 ton) or -15 to 105 °F (375-550 ton), high ambient 32 to 125 °F, wide ambient 0 to 125 °F
Leaving-water categories: standard 40 to 68 °F, low-temperature process below 40 °F, and ice-making 20 to 68 °F
productsAndServices.positioning: An independent sub-segment estimate places Trane second in global air-cooled chillers at 10.8% behind Carrier at 12.3% and ahead of Johnson Controls at 9.7% and Daikin at 8.4%. Air-cooled is the arrangement that trades efficiency for the removal of a cooling tower, its water and its chemistry — a trade increasingly settled by local water availability rather than by thermodynamics.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct and through the applied-equipment channel; packaged outdoor machines reduce the mechanical-room and installation scope.
productsAndServices.roadmap: ACS and ACX ship on R-454B, an A2L; ACR and Sintesis on R-513A, an A1 — the split reflects where the low-GWP transition has and has not required a flammability class change.

productsAndServices.name: Data-centre thermal management — chillers, CDUs and liquid cooling
productsAndServices.description: A dedicated data-centre range assembled largely through acquisition and reference-design partnership since late 2025. Four chillers are catalogued for the application: CenTraVac CDHH at 900-6,000+ tons (up to 21 MW) and CVHH at 850-2,600 tons (up to 9 MW), both on R-1233zd(E); an Ascend ACR data-centre variant up to 2 MW on R-1234ze with a factory-installed waterside economiser, a published Environmental Product Declaration and operation to 131 °F ambient; and the TCA oil-free magnetic-bearing air-cooled machine at 300-850 tons (up to 3 MW) on R-515B or R-1234ze. Beneath the plant, Trane sells coolant distribution units: the GigaModular CDU in 2.5 MW scalable building blocks validated to 14 MW, the CDU-1MW rated up to 1.35 MW with dual concurrently maintainable hot-swappable pumps, and an Asia-Pacific DCDA series. LiquidStack, acquired in March 2026, adds direct-to-chip and single- and two-phase immersion.
highlights: Portfolio claim, quoted verbatim: 'direct-to-chip liquid cooling distribution units that delivers up to 14MW of cooling capacity, the most in their size class'

GigaModular economics, quoted verbatim: 'Up to 25% CAPEX and floor space savings vs. traditional CDUs' and 'Up to 32% lower CapEx versus traditional row CDU deployments, depending on project design'; skid-mounted with front-only service access and operation to 50 °C ambient
Rapid Restart is offered on both the Ascend ACR data-centre chiller and the TCA — the feature that addresses the minutes-long gap between a power interruption and a plant making cooling again

The NVIDIA reference design was optimised in March 2026: a stated 10% improvement in overall thermal performance against the October 2025 design, freeing 22 MW of cooling capacity for IT power, delivered as two Trane Continuum Rubin DSX designs — a 250 MW duplex simplified system available now with extended free cooling and integrated heat recovery (14% thermal-system efficiency increase, 10% of heat rejection load to recovery), and a 1 GW magnetic-bearing air-cooled architecture using 3 MW air-cooled chiller units

The Eaton collaboration of August 2026 integrates Trane chillers, CDUs and controls with Eaton electrical infrastructure and claims up to 15% combined energy-efficiency gain, up to 80% less copper and up to 30% lower installation cost against conventional low-voltage designs

Disclosure boundary, stated rather than estimated: no data-centre revenue, growth rate, bookings figure or backlog split is disclosed anywhere. 'Data center' appears four times in the FY2025 10-K, all four inside an alphabetical products-and-services list, and the Q4 2025 and Q2 2026 earnings releases contain no data-centre commentary at all

What Trane does not sell here: no rear-door heat exchangers and no cold-plate products appear on the liquid-cooling pages, and no flow rates, approach-temperature figures or physical dimensions are published for either CDU
productsAndServices.positioning: ABI Research's January 2025 competitive ranking of thermal-management providers for data centres places Trane fifth, in the Mainstream tier, behind market leaders Vertiv and Johnson Controls and behind Schneider Electric and Daikin. Trade coverage positions the LiquidStack purchase as following rather than leading — Facilities Dive described it as 'the most recent deal between a major building systems OEM and a cutting-edge data center cooling technology provider, following moves last year by Schneider Electric and Johnson Controls' — notwithstanding Trane's minority stake in LiquidStack since 2023.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct, increasingly through published reference designs co-authored with NVIDIA and Eaton that specify the whole power-and-thermal chain rather than a single machine.
productsAndServices.roadmap: The 1 GW magnetic-bearing air-cooled Continuum Rubin DSX architecture was described in March 2026 as 'available soon'; the DCDA CDU series was expected in first China orders in Q1 2026.

productsAndServices.name: Commercial HVAC systems, controls and services
productsAndServices.description: The bulk of the business and the part that is not about data centres. Rooftop and applied air handling, terminal units, unitary and split systems, building management and controls, and an energy-services business that operates as a DOE-qualified energy services company. Services and maintenance contracts typically run 12 to 60 months and extended warranties up to five years; the company describes expanding recurring revenue through services and rental as an explicit growth strategy. Trane Cloud is the remote monitoring and management platform, and Trane AI Control — built on BrainBox AI, acquired in 2025 — is an artificial-intelligence service layered on Tracer SC+ controls.
highlights: Services scale, computed from the company's own disclosed line items rather than published as a percentage: services were $7,339.6M of $21,321.9M in FY2025, about 34.4%, up from about 32.9% in FY2024

AI Control claims, quoted verbatim: 'up to 25% reduction in HVAC energy consumption', 'Reduce your building's carbon footprint by up to 40%', and it 'requires no additional hardware'. The underlying BrainBox AI platform is stated as in use in over 14,000 buildings worldwide

Energy-savings performance guarantees are a real balance-sheet item: 'As of December 31, 2025, the Company has outstanding performance guarantees of approximately $1 billion related to completed energy savings contracts that extend from 2026-2049'

Four named performance obligations structure the revenue: equipment, contracting and installation, services and maintenance, and extended warranties. Revenue transferred at a point in time was approximately 79% in 2025

An exclusive US and Canada supply agreement with Valent, a Greenheck Group company, effective 18 May 2026, makes Trane the exclusive channel for Valent-branded dedicated outdoor air systems, value-added rooftop units and energy-recovery products
productsAndServices.positioning: Trane is an applied and commercial specialist rather than a volume air-conditioning player: it does not appear in independent top-five rankings of the global air-conditioning market, which are led by Daikin, Carrier, LG, Midea and Mitsubishi Electric. That distinction — engineered systems sold through engineers, not units sold through distribution — is the whole shape of the business.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct sales and service organisation, consulting-engineer specification, and a contractor and distributor channel for unitary products.
productsAndServices.roadmap: R&D of $347.6M in 2025 (from $309.6M in 2024 and $252.3M in 2023) is directed at energy efficiency, lower-GWP refrigerants, material reduction and design for circularity, with a Design for Sustainability module inside the new-product-development process.

productsAndServices.name: Residential HVAC — Trane and American Standard Heating & Air Conditioning
productsAndServices.description: Residential heating and cooling sold under two brands inside the Americas segment. The line completed a refrigerant transition to R-454B beginning with the 15 SEER2 heat pump, under a stated commitment to transition to low-GWP refrigerants in HVAC products by 2025. This is the part of the business that weakened in 2025.
highlights: The company's own read on the year, quoted verbatim from the FY2025 10-K: 'Residential markets have weakened considerably throughout 2025 due to navigating a regulatory refrigerant transition and softer consumer demand'
R-454B is described as offering 'nearly 78% lower' global warming potential than R-410A, and is a blend of R-32 and R-1234yf

Entity discipline: American Standard Heating & Air Conditioning is a Trane Technologies brand. American Standard Brands, the plumbing and bathroom-fixture business, has been a LIXIL Group subsidiary since 2013 and has no corporate connection — both descend from the 2007 break-up of American Standard Companies

A CPSC recall on 3 July 2025 covered approximately 5,000 gas/electric packaged units sold under both the Trane and American Standard brands between January 2024 and March 2025, for a fuel gas valve that can open unexpectedly; one report of gas leaking, remedy a free ignition-board replacement

Independent industry data frames the demand backdrop: AHRI recorded US shipments of central air conditioners and air-source heat pumps at 440,819 units in January 2026, down 29.2% year on year and an eighth consecutive monthly decline. Trane's own Q2 2026 commentary was sharply at odds with that — residential bookings up in the high twenties percent and revenue up low teens, with distributor inventory described as at appropriate levels
productsAndServices.positioning: A replacement-driven business whose demand is shaped by incentives and regulation as much as by weather. The early termination of the Section 25C residential efficiency credit for property placed in service after 31 December 2025 removes a point-of-sale subsidy from exactly this line.

productsAndServices.name: Thermo King — transport refrigeration
productsAndServices.description: The other strategic brand, and a different business on the same thermodynamics: refrigeration on a moving vehicle, which must carry its own power and survive vibration, road salt and wildly varying ambient conditions. Thermo King describes itself as the inventor of the transport refrigeration unit. Applications span trailers, trucks and vans, buses, rail cargo and passenger, and marine and shipping containers. Product families include Precedent trailer units (C and S Series, single- and multi-temperature), the T-90 Series diesel truck units, TriPac auxiliary power units and the ConnectedSuite telematics line. Thermo King is a brand and product line, not a reportable segment — its results are distributed across all three geographic segments.
highlights: The electrification line is branded evolve: 'A brand representing our electric transport refrigeration solutions for truck, trailer, bus, rail and marine applications'

Named electric products: the e1000, 'a fully electric transport refrigeration unit with zero emissions for large trucks'; the e200, CARB-approved for incentive programmes; the TriPac Envidia all-electric auxiliary power unit; the Precedent S-750i hybrid-electric trailer unit with integrated shore power; and the TE Series all-electric bus HVAC
Market condition, quoted verbatim from the FY2025 10-K: 'Transport refrigeration markets continue to experience weaker demand, particularly in the United States'

Independent check on the cycle: ACT Research reported US trailer orders of 13,500 in June 2026, down 35% month on month and 9% year on year, and characterises 2026 as rebalancing with backlog-to-build ratios below long-run averages — more equivocal than the company's own framing of a recovery in late 2026
productsAndServices.positioning: A cyclical business tied to freight and to fleet replacement rather than to construction, which is why it moves out of phase with commercial HVAC and why it dilutes the data-centre story in any consolidated number.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Dealer network and direct fleet sales.
productsAndServices.roadmap: Electrification across truck, trailer, bus, rail and marine, tied explicitly to the corporate commitment to reduce customer greenhouse gas emissions by one billion metric tons.

recentDevelopments.headline: Trane Technologies and Eaton publish an industry-first joint power-and-thermal reference design for AI data centres
recentDevelopments.read: The chiller vendor and the electrical vendor selling one engineered chain rather than two catalogues — and the only publicly stated commercial relationship Trane has in this ecosystem besides NVIDIA.

recentDevelopments.headline: Q2 2026: revenue $6,353.5M up 11%, adjusted continuing EPS $4.31 up 11%, backlog a record $12.1bn up 70%, Applied bookings up 130%
recentDevelopments.read: A fourth consecutive quarter of Applied bookings above 100% growth, with roughly half the backlog scheduled beyond 2027 — the constraint is now conversion timing rather than order intake.

recentDevelopments.headline: SVP and Chief Global Integrated Supply Chain Officer Mingxiao (Gary) Guo departs effective 1 August 2026
recentDevelopments.read: The 8-K states the departure did not arise from any disagreement over operations, policies, controls or financial matters; the timing sits alongside a tariff bill of roughly $200M a year and a Section 301 exclusion cliff in November.
recentDevelopments.source: Trane Technologies Form 8-K, 2026-07-20, as reported by TipRanks and Kalkine Media

recentDevelopments.headline: Donny Simmons, a 25-year veteran and most recently Group President Americas, named Chief Operating Officer effective 1 July 2026
recentDevelopments.read: Consolidates regional business units and operations under one officer; the leadership page now shows no Group President Americas, with separate presidents for Commercial HVAC Americas and Residential HVAC.

recentDevelopments.headline: 2025 Sustainability Report: 331 million metric tons of customer CO2e reduced since 2019 and operational emissions down 59%
recentDevelopments.read: About a third of the way to the Gigaton Challenge with four years to run, and ahead of the operational science-based target — the product roadmap and the commitment are the same roadmap.

recentDevelopments.headline: EPA finalises amendments loosening the Technology Transitions rule — the residential installation deadline is removed and industrial process chillers move to 1 January 2030
recentDevelopments.read: A demand-timing negative for a company that had already completed its transition: the forced-replacement catalyst in the applied line most exposed to data centres slips by up to four years.
recentDevelopments.source: Holland & Knight — EPA finalizes changes to Technology Transitions provisions, 2026-05-26

recentDevelopments.headline: Exclusive US and Canada supply agreement with Valent, a Greenheck Group company, for dedicated outdoor air systems and energy-recovery products
recentDevelopments.read: Buys a product line through the channel rather than through the balance sheet — an exclusivity rather than an acquisition.
recentDevelopments.source: Supply House Times — Trane Technologies and Valent announce exclusive supply agreement, 2026-05

recentDevelopments.headline: Q1 2026: revenue $4,969M, adjusted continuing EPS $2.63 up 7%, record backlog $10.7bn up more than 30% from year-end; guidance raised
recentDevelopments.read: Roughly $1bn of the backlog step came from the Stellar Energy acquisition rather than from organic orders — the distinction the headline number does not make.

relationships.note: Co-authored thermal-management reference designs for gigawatt-scale NVIDIA AI factories, engineered for the NVIDIA Omniverse DSX Blueprint.
relationships.context:
Announced 28 October 2025 as the industry's first comprehensive thermal-management system reference design at gigawatt scale, supporting GB300 NVL72 and next-generation Vera Rubin systems, with OpenUSD-based SimReady assets for digital-twin work.

Optimised on 16 March 2026 with a stated 10% improvement in overall thermal performance that frees 22 MW of cooling capacity for IT power, delivered as two Trane Continuum Rubin DSX designs — a 250 MW duplex system available then, and a 1 GW magnetic-bearing air-cooled architecture using 3 MW chiller units. LiquidStack, a Trane company since March 2026, subsequently launched a GigaModular CDU built to NVIDIA Vera Rubin specifications and scaling to 14 MW.

relationships.via: Trane Continuum Rubin DSX / Eaton Beam Rubin DSX
relationships.note: Joint reference design integrating Trane chillers, coolant distribution units and controls with Eaton electrical infrastructure for AI data centres.
relationships.context:
Announced 17 August 2026 and described by both companies as an industry first: 'a unified, intelligent system for power and cooling for next-generation data centers' replacing what the release calls a traditionally slow, manual and siloed design process. Claimed benefits against conventional low-voltage designs are up to 15% combined energy-efficiency gain, up to 80% less copper and up to 30% lower installation cost.

The design ships inside the Trane Continuum Rubin DSX and Eaton Beam Rubin DSX platforms. It is the clearest instance in this corpus of the power and thermal chains being sold as one engineered path rather than as two procurements — the pattern Vertiv's guide describes from the power side.

relationships.note: The market leader Trane competes with in data-centre thermal management, and the vendor whose guide in this app teaches the room-level chain.
relationships.context:
ABI Research's competitive ranking of thermal-management providers for data centres, published 30 January 2025, places Vertiv first as a Market Leader and Trane fifth in the Mainstream tier, with Johnson Controls, Schneider Electric and Daikin in between. Global Market Insights' data-centre chiller share table for 2025 runs the other way at the plant level — Trane second at 18.7%, Vertiv fifth at 8.1% — because the two companies are strong at different points in the same chain.

The pairing is the most useful comparison in the cooling half of this corpus: Vertiv sells the room and the distribution to the rack, Trane sells the machine that rejects the heat, and both have spent 2025 and 2026 buying their way toward the other's territory.
relationships.source: ABI Research — Vertiv and Johnson Controls take the lead in ABI Research's Thermal Management Providers for Data Centers competitive ranking (2025-01-30); Global Market Insights — Data Center Chillers Market (August 2026)

relationships.note: Ranked immediately above Trane in the Mainstream tier of the same thermal-management assessment, and the acquirer of CDU specialist Motivair.
relationships.context:
Schneider took a controlling interest in the direct-to-chip CDU vendor Motivair in September 2025 and launched a 2.5 MW MCDU-70 in January 2026. Facilities Dive positioned Trane's LiquidStack acquisition as following that move, describing it as 'the most recent deal between a major building systems OEM and a cutting-edge data center cooling technology provider, following moves last year by Schneider Electric and Johnson Controls'.

No supply, licensing or joint-development relationship between Trane and Schneider was found in any source. The link is curated as competitive because both are named in the same independent ranking and are acquiring into the same layer of the same chain.

policyExposure.exposure: The AIM Act requires US hydrofluorocarbon consumption to fall to 15% of the historic baseline by 2036, on an allowance schedule stepping down in 2026-2028, 2029-2033, 2034-2035 and 2036 onward. Trane's exposure is direct and dual: it must redesign products around lower-GWP fluids ahead of each step, and its residential line completed a transition to R-454B under a stated commitment to move to low-GWP refrigerants by 2025. The FY2025 10-K describes the risk in the company's own words without naming the statute: regulations 'could have a negative competitive impact on our company by requiring us to make costly changes to our products, or could make some of our existing HVAC and refrigeration products non-compliant or obsolete'.
policyExposure.mitigation: The commercial portfolio already ships on ultra-low-GWP fluids — R-514A and R-1233zd(E) at a stated GWP below two on CenTraVac, R-513A across much of the applied range — and $347.6M of 2025 R&D is directed in part at lower-GWP products. During the 2025 R-454B shortage the company increased factory pre-charging to reduce field refrigerant requirements.
policyExposure.source: Hunton Andrews Kurth — Status update on the AIM Act and EPA's HFC refrigerant regulations (2025-12-15); Trane Technologies FY2025 Form 10-K

policyExposure.exposure: The original rule took effect on 1 January 2025. EPA finalised amendments on 26 May 2026 that materially loosened it: the installation deadline for residential and light-commercial systems using refrigerant of 700 GWP or above manufactured before 1 January 2025 was removed entirely, supermarket refrigeration and cold-storage warehouses were extended to 1 January 2032, and semiconductor-manufacturing refrigeration and industrial process chillers moved from 2026 and 2028 to 1 January 2030. For Trane both changes are demand-timing negatives rather than compliance problems: the residential change reduces stranded-inventory risk for competitors still holding legacy stock, and the industrial-chiller delay removes a near-term forced-transition catalyst in the applied line most exposed to data centres.
policyExposure.source: Holland & Knight — EPA finalizes changes to Technology Transitions provisions (2026-05-26)

policyExposure.regime: A2L refrigerants and building codes (ASHRAE 15 and 34)
policyExposure.exposure: Most low-GWP replacements are classified A2L — low toxicity, mildly flammable — which brings leak detection, ventilation, charge limits and labelling into the machine room and into the building code. The 2024 editions of the IMC, IBC, IFC and IRC, keyed to ASHRAE 15 and 34 (2024), permit A2Ls with those requirements; the majority of US jurisdictions remain on the 2021 IMC, which does not reference A2Ls at all. A known gap under the 2024 IMC requires A2L refrigerant lines penetrating two or more floor or ceiling assemblies to run in a ventilated fire-rated shaft, with some jurisdictions adopting 2027 IMC language early to resolve it. Trane's exposure is uneven by product: R-454B lines (CGAM, Ascend ACS and ACX, most Thermafit, residential) are A2L; the CenTraVac line's R-1233zd(E) is explicitly A1 and nonflammable.
policyExposure.source: ICC Building Safety Journal — A2L refrigerants: latest challenges and opportunities; ACHR News — The code challenges behind the A2L transition

policyExposure.regime: Section 232 tariffs on steel, aluminium and copper
policyExposure.exposure: Restructured from 6 April 2026 into two tiers — 50% on articles wholly of the covered metals and 25% on derivative products substantially but not wholly of them — applied to the full customs value including derivatives, with the entirely-US-metal threshold relaxed from 95% to 85%. From 8 June 2026 residential HVAC systems and components were temporarily reduced to 15% ad valorem through 31 December 2027. Trane's quantified exposure is an estimated approximately $200M annual tariff cost after mitigation, with the CFO describing the enterprise impact moving from around 1.5 points to closer to two points.
policyExposure.mitigation: Strategic surcharges, stated by the company as the offset.
policyExposure.source: C.H. Robinson client advisories, 2026-04-06 and 2026-06-02; Trane Technologies Q1 2026 earnings call transcript, 2026-04-30

policyExposure.regime: Section 301 tariffs and the exclusion expiry
policyExposure.exposure: List rates run 25% on industrial machinery (Lists 1-3) and 7.5% on List 4A consumer goods. 178 product exclusions remain in force and expire at 23:59 ET on 9 November 2026, after which entries revert to the underlying list rate. The exclusions are narrowly drawn and specifically include rotary compressors within defined wattage ranges, DC blowers within defined size and output specifications, and electric motors within defined phase and horsepower limits — precisely the HVAC input categories. This is a dateable near-term cost event for the whole industry rather than for Trane alone.
policyExposure.source: Great Lakes Customs Law — Section 301 China exclusions in 2026: the 178 products still protected

policyExposure.exposure: The One Big Beautiful Bill Act terminated the Section 25C residential energy-efficiency credit early: it applies only to property placed in service before 31 December 2025, so equipment installed in 2026 does not qualify, and the trigger is placed-in-service rather than contract or deposit date. Section 25D for geothermal is gone on the same basis, and Section 179D, the commercial-buildings energy-efficiency deduction, expires for construction beginning after 30 June 2026. The 25C expiry removes a point-of-sale subsidy of up to $2,000 from residential replacement demand at the same time as AHRI shipment data showed an eighth consecutive monthly decline. The HEAR rebate programme survives because it was appropriated as grants to state energy offices rather than structured as a tax credit.

policyExposure.regime: Irish domicile and OECD Pillar Two
policyExposure.exposure: Trane Technologies plc is an Irish-incorporated public limited company with US operational headquarters in Davidson, North Carolina. Ireland applies a 12.5% trading-income corporation tax and a 25% passive rate, and groups with consolidated revenue at or above EUR 750M are subject to the 15% Pillar Two minimum effective rate, legislated in Ireland with effect from 1 January 2024. The company stated it included Pillar Two in its FY2024 estimated annual effective tax rate. Irish Revenue published updated guidance on 24 March 2026.
policyExposure.source: PwC Ireland corporate tax summary; KPMG TaxNewsFlash — Ireland: updated Pillar Two guidance (2026-04); Trane Technologies Q1 FY2024 Form 10-Q

policyExposure.regime: Asbestos liability — Aldrich Pump and Murray Boiler Chapter 11
policyExposure.exposure: Two indirect wholly owned subsidiaries created by a divisive merger under Texas law filed voluntary Chapter 11 petitions in June 2020 in the Western District of North Carolina, seeking a channelling injunction; pre-petition asbestos settlement and defence costs were reported at approximately $100M a year. All asbestos-related lawsuits against the two entities are stayed. The bankruptcy court denied motions to dismiss and certified a direct appeal; the Fourth Circuit affirmed in a published opinion in August 2025 (No. 24-1493) relying on its contemporaneous Bestwall holding, with a dissent, and denied rehearing en banc with six judges voting to grant. The court granted a motion to streamline liability-estimation proceedings on 17 December 2025, with Phase 1 of the estimation trial scheduled to begin the week of 10 August 2026. No outcome of that hearing was found as of 4 September 2026, and a Supreme Court petition in the Bestwall line (No. 25-1013) remains live.
policyExposure.source: US Court of Appeals for the Fourth Circuit, No. 24-1493 (August 2025); Haynes Boone (2024-02-29); Trane Technologies FY2025 Form 10-K

financials.commentary: Two things have to be held apart when reading this record. The first is the basis problem, and it is live: Trane reports both GAAP and adjusted continuing EPS, every published sell-side consensus located is adjusted-basis, and in FY2025 and Q1 2026 GAAP exceeded adjusted — the inverse of the usual direction. At least two outlets headlined the GAAP figure against an adjusted estimate in 2024 and 2025 quarters, manufacturing surprises of about six percentage points that do not exist. Every pairing above states its basis. A separate caution: one earnings-history tracker renders its forecast and actual columns transposed for this ticker, verified across four quarters. The second is that the backlog story is real but partly bought: the Q1 2026 step of more than 30% included roughly $1bn from the Stellar Energy acquisition, and backlog excludes residential product built in advance of order. Collection gap, stated rather than estimated: there is no data-centre revenue, growth rate or bookings disclosure of any kind, and no published split between commercial HVAC, residential HVAC and transport refrigeration. One retail outlet relayed an unattributed analyst estimate that data centres were about a fifth of commercial HVAC sales or about 10% of total revenue in 2025; it names no analyst and no firm, and it is recorded here as an estimate rather than used. Market data for context, at the close on 3 September 2026: share price $445.19, market capitalisation $97.95bn, 220.02M shares outstanding, dividend $4.20 at a 0.94% yield, trailing price/earnings 33.18, short interest 1.27% of float, and a consensus 12-month target of $526.99 across 24 analysts with a range of $422 to $575.

strategyRead: 1. **(High confidence)** We assess Trane is buying its way down the thermal chain rather than building down it, and doing so as a follower. Basis: a minority stake in LiquidStack taken in 2023 was converted to full ownership only in March 2026, after Schneider Electric took control of Motivair in September 2025 and Johnson Controls invested in Accelsius; Stellar Energy closed a month earlier for $553.4M gross. Facilities Dive described the LiquidStack purchase in exactly those terms — the most recent such deal, following moves the year before. The strategic logic is nonetheless sound: a chiller vendor that stops at the plant room sells into a shrinking share of the heat path as direct-to-chip cooling advances.

2. **(High confidence)** We assess the reference design, not the product catalogue, is now the company's principal go-to-market instrument in data centres. Basis: three published designs in ten months — NVIDIA in October 2025, an optimisation in March 2026 quantified as 22 MW of cooling capacity freed for IT power, and the Eaton power-and-thermal integration in August 2026 claiming 80% less copper and 30% lower installation cost. Selling a validated chain rather than a machine is how a vendor gets specified before the procurement starts, and it is the same pattern the power OEMs run.

3. **(Moderate confidence)** We assess the backlog is genuinely strong and partly mis-read. Basis: $12.1bn at Q2 2026 is 70% growth and about 57% of FY2025 revenue, against Carrier's $8bn at about 37% — a materially better coverage ratio. But roughly $1bn of the Q1 step was acquired rather than booked, about half the backlog is scheduled for 2027 and beyond, and backlog excludes residential product built in advance of order. The variable is conversion timing and capacity, not demand. We found no published analyst work questioning backlog durability, cancellation terms or the organic-versus-acquired split, and that absence is itself worth noting.

4. **(Moderate confidence)** We assess the company is running two businesses on opposite cycles and that this is under-appreciated in any single headline number. Basis: Americas commercial HVAC bookings up 50% in Q2 2026 against residential markets the company itself describes as having 'weakened considerably throughout 2025', AHRI industry shipments down 29.2% year on year in January 2026 on an eighth consecutive monthly decline, and transport refrigeration explicitly weak with ACT Research reporting US trailer orders down 35% month on month in June 2026. Trane's own Q2 residential commentary — bookings up in the high twenties percent — is sharply at odds with the industry data, and that divergence is unreconciled.

5. **(Moderate confidence)** We assess the refrigerant transition has flipped from a tailwind to a timing headwind. Basis: the company completed its commercial migration to ultra-low-GWP fluids and its residential migration to R-454B ahead of the schedule, and then EPA's May 2026 amendments removed the residential installation deadline entirely and pushed industrial process chillers from 2026 and 2028 to 2030. A company that transitioned early loses the forced-replacement catalyst it had priced in, while competitors holding legacy inventory gain relief. Against that, the January 2026 leak-repair rule for appliances with 15 lb or more of charge enlarges the recurring-service base, which is the higher-margin revenue.

6. **(Low confidence)** We assess the most conspicuous gap in the public record is the absence of a single named data-centre customer. Basis: across an exhaustive check of hyperscalers, colocation operators, AIDC developers and the general contractors that build for them, no source states a commercial relationship between Trane Technologies and any of them; the only two publicly stated relationships in this ecosystem are the NVIDIA and Eaton reference designs. For a company whose backlog growth is attributed to data-centre orders, that is either exceptional customer confidentiality or a sign that the orders route through contractors and developers rather than through named end users. Both readings are consistent with the evidence and neither is established.

7. **(Low confidence)** We assess the asbestos structure remains the largest single unquantified liability in the file. Basis: Aldrich Pump and Murray Boiler have been in Chapter 11 since June 2020 on pre-petition costs reported at about $100M a year; the Fourth Circuit affirmed in August 2025 but with a dissent and an en banc denial on a six-vote split; Phase 1 of the liability-estimation trial was scheduled for the week of 10 August 2026 and no outcome was found; and a Supreme Court petition in the related Bestwall line is live. An adverse ruling on the divisive-merger structure would reach this company directly.
